pages.text: A basket brimmed with freshly washed towels. Kota helped by rolling each one into a ball. A round pile grew on the shelf.
A tanuki guest reached for a towel after his bath. One rolled out—and the others tumbled after it!
Kota picked them up and rolled them again. "These towels won't listen!" Their cheeks puffed out.
Dad spread a towel flat. "Let's build a towel mountain. Flat towels make a steady mountain." Kota held the corners.
Fold in half, then in half again. A neat square settled on the shelf without rolling away.
Kota placed one square on another. The towel mountain grew taller and taller.
The tanuki guest pulled off the top towel. The mountain stayed neat! "Much better!" Kota's tail lifted.
"I built that mountain!" Kota wriggled their nose. The guest wiped Kota's cheek with his towel. "Now its owner has a clean face, too."
Kota made three mountains, matching all the corners. "One, fold in half. Two, fold again. Three, set it down!" No more rolling balls.
Dad patted Kota's back beside the next mountain. "A little care makes everything fluffier." "Fold, fold, a fluffy mountain!" Kota smiled.
